title: Action de Galois sur Teichmüller : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting: Σ = P^1(C) with three marked points R_0, R_1, R_∞ on the real equator Σ_R, so the punctured sphere Σ* is P^1 minus {0,1,∞}. Σ̃ is the compact bordered surface obtained by removing small discs around the R_i (equivalently, the real-oriented blow-up). Γ = S_3 × {1,τ} has order 12, where τ is complex conjugation (reflection in the equator); Γ is the automorphism group of the map ('carte') given by the equator and the three points.

On the previous page, the pinning isomorphisms Ψ_i^{ω,ε} : π_{0,3} → π_1(Σ̃, P_ε) were computed with base points at the poles P_ε (centres of the two hemispheres/faces) and at the points Q_i (edge midpoints). Grothendieck then says the crucial base points for the intended work are those near the holes R_i, because the monodromy around them is what matters.

On this page he introduces such base regions. The barycentric subdivision of the map gives 12 flag triangles D̃_r = P_ε Q_i R_{ωi}, indexed by r = (i, ω, ε) = (edge, orientation/end, hemisphere). Γ acts simply transitively on them. Cut down to Σ̃, each triangle becomes a quadrilateral P_ε Q R S, where S is a point on the boundary circle around the puncture. On the standard sphere this is P_+ Q_∞ R_0^+ S_0^+.

To get a neighbourhood of the flag, he reflects D̃_r across its three sides:
- the equator side, by τ;
- the side through P_ε and Q_i, by σ̃_i;
- the side through P_ε and R, by σ̃_{ωi}.
On the standard model these correspond to τ, σ̃_∞, σ̃_0. Formula (41) sets Σ̃_r = D̃_r ∪ τ(D̃_r) ∪ σ̃_i(D̃_r) ∪ σ̃_{ωi}(D̃_r), a region bounded by a single contour through both poles (made explicit on the next page).

The next page shows why. The Σ̃_r are simply connected and permuted simply transitively by Γ. So one gets fundamental groups π_r = π_1(Σ̃; Σ̃_r) based at a simply connected region rather than at a point, with canonical transition isomorphisms φ_r to π_1(Σ̃, P_ε) and pinnings Ψ_r : π_{0,3} → π_r.

In modern terms, these are combinatorial/topological stand-ins for tangential base points at the punctures, with 12 of them rather than Deligne's 6 because the hemisphere is also recorded. They are arranged equivariantly for Γ, so that the action of Γ (and later Galois) on the pinned π_{0,3} can be computed through local monodromy at the R_i.
errors: Formula (41) as written ends with σ̃_{ωi}(Σ̃_r), which is circular. It should read σ̃_{ωi}(D̃_r); this is a slip of the pen, also visible in the manuscript.

The listed contour is garbled in the transcription. Judging from the next page, it is a single closed contour through both poles, P_ε Q_{ω'i} R S R S P_{ε'} Q_i R_{ω'i} S_{ω'i} P_ε, not two separate contours.

Some looseness in what Σ_r, Σ̃_r and D̃_r denote (triangle versus enlarged region). There is no mathematical error: the union of a triangle with its reflections across its three sides, cut by the discs, is indeed simply connected.

ideas.what: Using the 12 flags of the barycentric subdivision of the real 'carte' (equator plus 0,1,∞) as an S_3×Z/2-torsor of base objects
ideas.modern_name: flags of a dessin d'enfant / barycentric subdivision; automorphism group of a real regular map
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (barycentric subdivision of maps, cartes and flags)

ideas.what: Simply connected base regions near the punctures, chosen Γ-equivariantly, as substitutes for point base points to compute monodromy around the holes R_i
ideas.modern_name: tangential base points (Deligne) / fundamental groupoid with symmetric family of base points
ideas.usually_credited_to: Deligne 1989 (Le groupe fondamental de la droite projective moins trois points); Ihara; Grothendieck's Esquisse mentions groupoids with symmetric families of base points
ideas.where_published: Esquisse discusses fundamental groupoids relative to well-chosen base points; the exact flag-region construction does not seem published

ideas.what: Fundamental group relative to a simply connected subspace, π_1(X; U), with transition isomorphisms φ_r
ideas.modern_name: fundamental group based at a contractible subspace / groupoid restricted to a set of base points
ideas.usually_credited_to: folklore; R. Brown (groupoids on sets of base points)

ideas.what: Reflections in the sides of a flag triangle (τ, σ̃_i, σ̃_{ωi}) generating the Γ-action
ideas.modern_name: Coxeter/reflection description of the flag group of a regular map

missed.claim: Before Deligne's tangential base points (1989), Grothendieck replaces point base points by Γ-equivariant simply connected 'flag regions' touching the boundary circles around 0,1,∞. This explicitly serves to see monodromy at the punctures. There are 12 such regions (6 tangential directions × 2 hemispheres), forming an S_3×{1,τ}-torsor. It is a topological precursor of tangential base points that also builds in complex conjugation.
missed.quote: ce sont les points R_i^ω qui sont les plus cruciaux ... Je vais réparer cette négligence ... des régions Σ̃_r = Σ̃_i^{ω,ε} associées aux régions r=(i,ω,ε)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is a documentary priority/precursor point for the tangential-base-point formalism in the anabelian and GT setting. The inclusion of τ (12 rather than 6) matches later work on real structures and complex conjugation in GT. The construction itself would not be new to specialists.

deep.surprise_reason: A careful, equivariant construction of base regions near the punctures, clearly motivated by local monodromy. It anticipates tangential base points, but the idea is natural and close in spirit to known Grothendieck themes (Esquisse). There is no new theorem here.
transcription_corrections: First line likely reads 'plus des D̃_∞, Π_∞ et D̃_i, Π_i' (continuing 'en introduisant, en plus des ...' from the previous page), not 'par des Σ̃_{∞,Π_ω}'.
'ce qui revient au même, de (J̃, J̄)' – the symbols appear to be script J with tilde/bar decorations.
In (41) the last term in the manuscript is indeed written σ̃_{ωi}(Σ_r) (author slip for D̃_r).
The contour should be read as one closed path through P_ε and P_{ε'}: 'P_ε Q_{ω'i} R^{ω'}_{ωi} S^ε_i R^ω_{ωi} S^{ε'}_i P_{ε'} Q_i R_{ω'i} S_{ω'i} P_ε'.
'Le "trace" sur Σ̃ induit d'un tel triangle est un quadrilatère' – the '{+sur Σ̃+}' insertion replaces the earlier text.
